title: Strings with a radix prefix and a sign after it
notes: None of these is a number under the Core schema or YAML 1.1, so they are strings. Some readers take them as numbers all the same: gopkg.in/yaml.v3 reads `0b-1` as -1 and `0o+7` as 7, because it hands the text to a number parser that accepts a sign after the prefix and underscores. A string is therefore quoted when it has a 0x, 0o or 0b prefix with a sign after it. The Core-schema reading (loose) is the specification. The reading under YAML 1.1 and the number forms that some common readers accept (strict) is a writing convention of the family: a string is written plain only when it reads as that same string there too.

provenance.reference: Strings such as 0b-1, 0o+7 and 0b-1_0 written without quotes; one common reader reads 0b-1 as the number -1.
